title: How init drops and recreates rates
description: Application code may not run DDL or open a driver; schema is provisioned by the DATABASE step. Options: a declared reset operation that removes every row, or raw DROP/CREATE.

options.label: Declared repository reset removes all rows

title: Application package name
description: Application modules live in the package fxrates_app (config, ecb, fetch, rates), alongside the reserved cli, app_server, and persistence packages.

title: Stub seam for the ECB download
description: fetch isolates the network behind fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive(url) so tests patch one function; the timeout is chosen by the builder because the sources state none.
system_choice: fxrates_app.fetch.download_archive is the only network call

title: Validator exposed as a module function
description: LOAD-001 delivers a parser/validator function; the load command that exits 3 is registered in LOAD-002, which also proves rejection end to end with the supplied bad file.
system_choice: fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history raises RejectedFile; load maps it to exit 3

title: Static route ordering for /rates/latest
description: /rates/latest must be matched before /rates/{date} so latest is not treated as a malformed date.

title: Test runner invocation and pytest placement
description: Declared pytest in the uv dev dependency group rather than runtime dependencies, and bin/test.sh calls .venv/bin/pytest -q directly instead of sourcing activate (sourcing trips set -u in the venv activate script). Both keep the declared test_command pytest -q. Acceptable?
system_choice: Declared pytest in the uv dev dependency group rather than runtime dependencies, and bin/test.sh calls .venv/bin/pytest -q directly instead of sourcing activate (sourcing trips set -u in the venv activate script). Both keep the declared test_command pytest -q. Acceptable?

title: Launcher working directory
description: The fxrates launcher changes into the application root before running python -m cli, matching bin/test.sh and keeping the default data/app.db path stable. Relative file paths passed by callers therefore resolve against the root. Acceptable, or should the launcher preserve the caller's cwd?
system_choice: The fxrates launcher changes into the application root before running python -m cli, matching bin/test.sh and keeping the default data/app.db path stable. Relative file paths passed by callers therefore resolve against the root. Acceptable, or should the launcher preserve the caller's cwd?

title: validate signature and registry check
description: validate takes an optional registered collection so commands with a handler are accepted without importing the dispatcher (avoids a circular import). With no argument it behaves as validate(argv) in the spec. Is that acceptable, or should the registry check move into dispatcher.main?
system_choice: validate takes an optional registered collection so commands with a handler are accepted without importing the dispatcher (avoids a circular import). With no argument it behaves as validate(argv) in the spec. Is that acceptable, or should the registry check move into dispatcher.main?

title: Unknown currency and zero stored rate
description: A currency with no stored rate on the effective date (not EUR) returns 404. A stored rate of zero returns 422 instead of a 500 from division by zero. The spec did not name either status. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: A currency with no stored rate on the effective date (not EUR) returns 404. A stored rate of zero returns 422 instead of a 500 from division by zero. The spec did not name either status. Is that acceptable?

title: Check order for an unknown currency combined with a malformed bound
description: Bound validation (422) runs before the currency lookup (404), so a request with both an unknown code and a malformed bound answers 422. The spec does not state which applies first. Is that acceptable, or should unknown currency take precedence?
system_choice: Bound validation (422) runs before the currency lookup (404), so a request with both an unknown code and a malformed bound answers 422. The spec does not state which applies first. Is that acceptable, or should unknown currency take precedence?

title: Response fields for this block
description: The response carries currency, base, count, and points. count is included because the history acceptance criterion asserts it. min, max, and mean are omitted and left for FEATURE-HistoryStats. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: The response carries currency, base, count, and points. count is included because the history acceptance criterion asserts it. min, max, and mean are omitted and left for FEATURE-HistoryStats. Is that acceptable?

title: Empty input and header-only files
description: The spec does not say how to treat empty input. I reject empty text as having no header. A header-only file with no data rows is accepted and yields an empty list. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: The spec does not say how to treat empty input. I reject empty text as having no header. A header-only file with no data rows is accepted and yields an empty list. Is that acceptable?

title: Repeated currency code in the header
description: The spec does not cover duplicate header codes. I reject the file, because two columns with the same code would produce duplicate (date, currency) keys. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: The spec does not cover duplicate header codes. I reject the file, because two columns with the same code would produce duplicate (date, currency) keys. Is that acceptable?

title: Indexes derived from the persistence declaration
description: The rendered schema indexes rates(date); rates(currency, date). Each is implied by the declaration — a foreign key is looked up by its child column, and a read pattern's Input fields are the predicate it filters on. Declare an `- INDEX (...)` bullet in DATABASE.md for any index this does not cover.
